clue.text: Cockney hunted down on policeman's first beat

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the hunted piece is placed after the policeman's letter
first asks for just the opening letter of the word policeman's
a Cockney speaker famously drops the initial aitch, so the H of the synonym goes

parts.note: to be hunted down is to be hounded

explanation.surface: A London bobby out on his first beat, chasing down a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' signals dropping the H, giving OUNDED; 'on' sets that after the P. 'beat' looks like the policeman's patch but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat something repeatedly is to have pounded it, a straightforward synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Puritan outfit under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the outfit below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: A puritan dressed in a costume under pressure to conform.
explanation.definitionFit: A prig is a self-righteously moralistic person, much like a puritan.

clue.text: Remarkable Scots centre missed by world heritage guardians

indicators.note: centre missed by means the middle pair of letters drop out

parts.note: UNESCO designates and protects World Heritage Sites

explanation.surface: A notable Scottish site overlooked by the World Heritage body.
explanation.definitionFit: Unco is a Scots word meaning unusual or remarkable.

clue.text: Make use of frame one trimmed

parts.note: to frame a document is to draw it up

indicators.note: trimmed means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A picture frame with one piece cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw upon resources is to make use of them, an idiom.

clue.text: Duke, working men's benefactor

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who funds a working men's club.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods, so is a benefactor.

clue.text: Many trousers briefly removed

parts.note: bags is old British slang for loose trousers

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word to be cut short by its final letter

parts.note: removed means off, as in taken off

explanation.surface: Someone's trousers have been quickly taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks OFF to OF. BAGS is British slang for wide trousers (as in Oxford bags).
explanation.definitionFit: Bags of is informal British for a great quantity, so it stands for many or lots of.

clue.text: First man from south to join a king's fleet

parts.note: R is rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: from south means read upward in this down clue

parts.note: Adam is the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: The first man from the south joins a king's naval force.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, most famously the Spanish one.

clue.text: Preserve place for wine dispenser at table

parts.note: to salt food is to preserve it
a cellar is where wine is stored

explanation.surface: Keeping a spot for wine to be poured at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar is the small container that dispenses salt at a dining table.

clue.text: Where crops may be grown after dams burst close to Paris?

indicators.note: burst means the letters break apart and re-form
close to takes the final letter of Paris

explanation.surface: Fields flood near Paris after dams give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a time word but is anagram fodder, scrambled by 'burst' along with the dams.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmsteads are farms with their buildings and land, the places that produce crops.

clue.text: Entering taverns after tea, I'll be bound

indicators.note: entering means the tea and I go into the taverns

parts.note: taverns are inns

indicators.note: after places the I following the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A drinker announces a pub crawl after their cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The I does double duty: it is part of the wordplay and also opens the definition 'I'll be bound', a setter's deliberate reuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in chains is shackled, so they are bound, as the speaker will be.

clue.text: Singular athlete, one accustomed to beam

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a miler is an athlete who runs the mile

explanation.surface: A lone runner who balances on a gymnastics beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' suggests gymnastics but means to grin.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually beams, i.e. smiles broadly, is a smiler.

clue.text: Tenor's last note upset acoustic device

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of the word Tenor's
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read upward

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A singer's final note is spoilt by the sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor's last' is R (Tenor's ends in S, so the possessive is set aside); 'upset' turns BREVE into EVERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echo effect device used with amplifiers.

clue.text: Spaces aboard for officers' suits?

definitions.meaning: the quarterdeck is the part of a ship's deck reserved for officers
each suit in a pack of cards is a quarter of the deck

explanation.definitionFit: A deck of cards has four suits, so each is a quarter, while a quarterdeck is the officers' area of a warship.

clue.text: Sailors attending course find something to keep them going

parts.note: Epsom is a racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby
salts are old sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors at the races need something to sustain them.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is the English racecourse that stages the Derby. 'keep them going' is a joke on bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are taken as a laxative, keeping the bowels moving.

clue.text: Possible source of firing put poacher off

indicators.note: off means the letters are disordered, gone off from their arrangement

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper scares off a poacher before he can shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchpaper is the fuse paper lit to set off a firework.

clue.text: Marked word such as we initially check with editor

parts.note: we is an example of a pronoun

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of check

explanation.surface: An editor checks a royal or editorial 'we' in some copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronounced means very noticeable or distinct, a sense close to marked.

clue.text: Nothing titillating? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of its final letter

parts.note: naughty can mean mildly titillating, risque

explanation.surface: Something not quite risque enough to titillate.
explanation.definitionFit: Naught is an archaic word for nothing.

clue.text: Yankee cracking clue oddly rejected solution

indicators.note: cracking means the Y breaks into the remaining letters
oddly rejected discards the odd-placed letters of clue, keeping the even ones

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A solver rejects a clue, perhaps an American one, they could not crack.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping C and U from 'clue' leaves LE, which Y splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is an alkaline chemical solution used in soap-making and cleaning.

clue.text: Gunners turning up refreshed, ran in

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading upward

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
rested means refreshed

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrive refreshed and run inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran in' is informal for took into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone in is slang for to arrest them.

clue.text: Aquatic mammal seabird caught

indicators.note: caught means heard, so the seabird is taken by ear

parts.note: the auk is a diving seabird

explanation.surface: A sea creature caught a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: AUK and ORC only sound alike in non-rhotic accents such as standard British English, where the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An orc is a dictionary name for the orca or killer whale, a marine mammal.

clue.text: Where deal may be had by mad ruler on the move?

indicators.note: on the move means the letters are shifted about into new positions

explanation.surface: A crazed monarch travelling around the country cuts a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a bargain but is timber: deal is pine or fir planking.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberyard sells timber, and deal is a softwood timber sold there.

clue.text: Poet's 'void land south of river'

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of places the land letters below the river

parts.note: the Arno is the river of Florence and Pisa

indicators.note: void means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of land

explanation.surface: A poet's line describing an empty landscape by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Arnold was a Victorian poet, author of Dover Beach.

clue.text: Emotive outcome of corruption at police HQ?

definitions.meaning: ... can describe a highly emotional atmosphere

definitions.text: outcome of corruption at police HQ?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., a superintendent charged after corruption is found

explanation.definitionFit: A supercharged atmosphere is intensely charged with feeling, close to emotive; a superintendent is a senior police officer.

clue.text: Sleep with sailor in bunk?

indicators.note: in places the sailor inside the nonsense word

parts.note: bunk means nonsense, rot
OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: Sharing a bunk with a sailor for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they settle to sleep, so to roost is to sleep.

clue.text: Served up duck with potato dressing

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the letters are read upward

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O
yam is a sweet potato

explanation.surface: A dish of duck and potatoes served with a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo, short for mayonnaise, is a salad dressing.

clue.text: Last of pickers still to grade fruit

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: The fruit pickers' final job is still to grade the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloe is the small dark fruit of the blackthorn.

clue.text: Particle quietly splitting gave the game away

indicators.note: splitting means the soft letter breaks the phrase apart

parts.note: let on means to reveal a secret
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone quietly let slip a secret about particle physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A lepton is an elementary particle, such as the electron, in physics.

clue.text: Number of customers in time to pay for trip

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for something
to trip is to fall

explanation.surface: Getting somewhere on time to pay for a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey but is a stumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers measure footfall as the count of shoppers entering over a given period.

clue.text: Plodded into the Home Counties and moved on apace

indicators.note: into means the plodding word goes inside the region's letters

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East, abbreviated SE
trod means walked heavily, plodded

explanation.surface: A walker trudged into the countryside near London, then sped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: To stride is to walk with long brisk steps, so strode means went along briskly.

clue.text: Immature swimmer bit staff

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
a pole is a staff or rod

explanation.surface: A young swimmer took a bite out of a staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larva of a frog or toad, which swims before maturing.
